name: Macrophage or Histiocytic Tumor

criteria.description: Histopathological identification of malignant histiocytic cells with characteristic morphology
Positive immunohistochemical staining for histiocytic markers (CD68, CD163) and negative for lymphoid and dendritic cell markers
Exclusion of other hematologic malignancies such as lymphoma or dendritic cell sarcoma
Presence of a mass lesion with or without systemic symptoms

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation with immunophenotyping demonstrating histiocytic lineage and exclusion of other malignancies
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of morphology, immunophenotyping, and clinical exclusion of other entities.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Localized tumor mass with histiocytic morphology
pathognomonic.notes: Typically presents as a solitary or multifocal mass
searchTerms: localized tumor with immune cell features

pathognomonic.symptomName: Immunohistochemical positivity for CD68 and CD163
searchTerms: tumor cells positive for CD68 and CD163 markers

common.symptomName: B symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss)

common.notes: Enlarged lymph nodes may be present
Enlargement of liver and spleen in disseminated disease

searchTerms: bone marrow infiltration by abnormal cells
blood cell production affected by marrow involvement

occasional.notes: Skin involvement can occur in some cases

occasional.symptomName: Respiratory symptoms due to pulmonary involvement
occasional.notes: Cough or dyspnea if lungs are affected
searchTerms: respiratory symptoms due to lung involvement

occasional.notes: Rare but possible in disseminated disease
searchTerms: neurological deficits from brain or spinal involvement
nerve problems due to CNS disease
weakness or sensory loss from CNS

rare.symptomName: Cardiovascular compromise due to cardiac infiltration

searchTerms: vision issues due to eye disease

rare.symptomName: Endocrine dysfunction secondary to hypothalamic or pituitary infiltration

laboratory: Anemia and cytopenias on complete blood count
imaging: CT or MRI showing mass lesions in lymph nodes, soft tissue, or organs
genetic: No consistent genetic mutation identified; occasional clonal abnormalities reported
other: Histopathology showing large pleomorphic histiocytic cells
Immunohistochemistry positive for CD68, CD163, lysozyme

distinguishingFeatures: Positive for follicular dendritic cell markers (CD21, CD35)

redFlags: Rapidly enlarging mass with systemic B symptoms
references: Swerdlow SH, et al. WHO Classification of Tumours of Haematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues, 2017.
Feldman AL, et al. Histiocytic Sarcoma: A Review. Arch Pathol Lab Med. 2017.
